title: Bluecrest pilot governance gate - SSO, audit logs, retention
summary: Weekly pilot governance gate focusing on SSO onboarding, audit log exports, and data retention policy. Agreed on SAML metadata exchange, 90-day default retention with option for export to customer S3, and a SOC 2 artifacts handoff next week.

Retention policy and legal hold options

transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 37 min
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Morgan (Bluecrest Head of Security), Priya Singh (Eng Manager), Tom Wu (DevOps)

Auto-summary: quick governance gate to unblock next phase of POC; main items SSO, audit logs export, retention and SOC2 evidence sharing.

[00:00] Maya Lin: hey everyone, thanks for joining — good to see you all, let's do a quick round, we'll cover SSO, audit logs and retention then list out next steps.
[00:22] Alex Morgan: thanks, Maya. we've got Priya and Tom here, I'm Alex. security's main asks are: can we get SSO working end-to-end, ensure audit logs ship to our SIEM, and that retention defaults align with our comps.
[01:05] Raj Patel: great, we'll show what we did this week and then walk through the config. quick note, transcription might mangle some of the infra terms like "KV cache" sometimes it comes out as "K V cake" so just flag if that happens.
[02:10] Priya Singh: ha, yeah. small ask: for role mappings we'd like to map to our internal AD groups, SCIM would help with provisioning.
[03:05] Raj Patel: perfect — Redwood supports SAML for authentication and SCIM for provisioning. for the POC we've got an IdP test flow with a temporary metadata file. we'll send the canonical metadata after this call. The SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows both work, but the default redirect timing in our hosted flow is 2.5s, so if you're measuring timeouts please allow a 5s window at first. (laughs)
[05:00] Tom Wu: for audit logs, we need to know fields and whether we can get raw event stream — events should include user_id, token_id, route, model_id, timestamp, and the decision reason for fallbacks. does Redwood expose those fields?
[05:45] Raj Patel: yes, we emit an event schema — I'll paste the schema in the deck notes but top-level fields are user_id, request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_in/out, decision_trace. a couple notes: model names sometimes get normalized in the export, e.g., "redwood-gg-base" might appear slightly different in some places.
[06:40] Alex Morgan: normalization is fine, just need consistency. also need tamper-evidence — can logs be signed or exported to our S3 with server-side encryption?
[07:20] Maya Lin: yes, we support log export to a customer-owned S3 bucket and we can apply SSE-KMS. for SIEM you can also do syslog over TLS or Kinesis Firehose.
[08:15] Priya Singh: what's the latency impact of enabling full audit logging? we can't add more than 5% token latency.
[09:00] Raj Patel: in our tests enabling verbose audit fields adds negligible CPU overhead on the control plane; the per-request token path isn't changed. network egress to your SIEM could add tail latency if you call a synchronous endpoint, but we stream logs asynchronously. in practice we saw <1% p50 difference, p99 might vary depending on network.
[10:10] Tom Wu: ok, asynchronous export is fine. does Redwood support guaranteed delivery to Kinesis with retries? we need at-least-once semantics.
[10:50] Raj Patel: yes, Firehose / Kinesis integrations have retry and buffering, we also keep a local enqueue with TTL of 48 hours before dropping, configurable for Dedicated. for hosted customers default is 24 hours queue TTL.
[12:00] Alex Morgan: retention policy: Bluecrest wants 90 days by default, with an option to lower or extend for audited records. can you do legal hold to prevent deletion?
[12:35] Maya Lin: default retention in the POC tenant can be set to 90 days; we can enable a legal hold API to lock specific request IDs for 7 years if needed for litigation, but that'll require dedicated config and a different retention contract.
[13:20] Priya Singh: please note we will classify some transcripts as PII and they have to follow stricter deletion rules. can we tag requests and have per-tag retention?
[13:55] Raj Patel: we support metadata tagging on requests and per-tag retention policies for Dedicated and Private deployments. for hosted we can set tenant-level retention and we do support policy-based export for selective retention — e.g., forward PII-tagged entries to your S3 and purge from Redwood after 30 days.
[15:30] Tom Wu: re: SSO, we prefer SCIM auto-provisioning. will group de-provisioning immediately cut access or is there a delay? we need near-immediate revocation.
[16:10] Raj Patel: SCIM provisioning reflects changes within 60s in our standard config; for Dedicated we can push to near-real-time but depends on downstream IdP. immediate revocation for sessions uses short-lived tokens and we can revoke active tokens via our admin API.
[17:45] Alex Morgan: SOC 2: we saw some artifacts last week but need the mapping to controls for the upcoming audit. can you provide the SOC 2 snapshot and a mapping to CC6/CC7 type controls?
[18:20] Raj Patel: yes, I'll assemble a SOC 2 supplement that maps our controls to the audit criteria. it'll include the log retention, key management (we use AWS KMS for hosted; for Private we support customer-managed HSM), incident response playbook, and evidence locations.
[19:10] Maya Lin: note I'll put that in the shared folder and mark it restricted.
[20:00] Priya Singh: small concern: some model variants fall back to smaller models during capacity pressure — we need to ensure fallback decisions are logged with reason codes so auditing can reconstruct decisions.
[20:40] Raj Patel: we log fallback_reason with a code and description. for the export we'll include those fields. sometimes our model variant names change between infra releases, hope that's okay but we will pin versions for your pilot.
[21:30] Tom Wu: pinning versions is important. also, encryption in transit for cache/KV — do we have TLS between Redwood runtime and any external caches?
[22:10] Raj Patel: yes, internal traffic is TLS. if you configure an external KV store we'll recommend TLS and mutual auth. again, some transcription may show wrong acronyms — e.g., K V cache -> KV cache.
[23:05] Alex Morgan: about audit log format, can we get a sample line?
[23:30] Raj Patel: sure — sample: {timestamp, request_id, user_id, model_id, variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, fallback_reason, route, region}. I'll paste a sanitized CSV after the call.
[24:20] Priya Singh: question: can we mask user PII in logs while preserving deterministic IDs for tracing?
[24:55] Raj Patel: yes — we can hash user IDs before export with a salt you manage; that keeps links across logs but obfuscates raw PII.
[25:40] Tom Wu: about SIEM ingestion — we prefer S3 + Athena for ad-hoc queries over syslog. is there a cost or lag tradeoff?
[26:10] Maya Lin: S3 export + manifest is usually the most reliable and economical; syslog is lower-latency but requires always-on ingestion. Firehose can write to S3 with buffering and compression; expected lag is on the order of seconds to low minutes depending on buffer size.
[27:00] Alex Morgan: what's the approval process to move from hosted POC to Dedicated for compliance? we want the expected timeline.
[27:35] Raj Patel: typical timeline is 4-6 weeks once we sign a Dedicated contract: infra provisioning, KMS key exchange, VPC peering or private link setup, and a cutover run. we can compress to 3 weeks with parallel work if you commit to a lead from your side for network changes.
[28:10] Priya Singh: ok. last thing: audit log retention and retrieval SLA — can you promise retrieval for up to 2 years for eDiscovery?
[28:45] Raj Patel: for hosted we can retain and export up to 1 year by default; for 2 years and eDiscovery-grade retention we recommend Dedicated or Private and add the governance add-on.
[29:30] Maya Lin: circling back to action items: we'll send SAML metadata, Raj will send SOC2 artifacts and schema, Tom will provide SIEM endpoint, Priya will confirm tag-based retention.
[30:00] Alex Morgan: sounds good. one more tiny ask: need a one-page diagram of data flow for the auditor, showing where logs land and who has access.
[30:30] Raj Patel: I'll generate a simplified diagram with flow: client -> Redwood runtime -> audit log enqueue -> export (S3/Kinesis/syslog) and annotate encryption and key ownership.
[31:20] Priya Singh: and include the legal hold flow, please.
[31:55] Raj Patel: yes.
[32:40] Maya Lin: any blockers?
[33:05] Tom Wu: none from me; just need to get the SIEM details.
[33:25] Alex Morgan: no blockers; need SOC2 mapping.
[33:40] Priya Singh: fine.
[34:20] Maya Lin: next steps recap — SAML metadata (Maya) by 11/6, SIEM details (Tom) by 11/5, SOC2 mapping + schema (Raj) by 11/10, retention confirmation (Priya) by 11/8, and we'll schedule the latency run for week of 11/9.
[35:05] Alex Morgan: perfect, thanks all.
[35:30] Raj Patel: thanks everyone, I'll share the sample logs and diagram after.
[36:10] Maya Lin: thanks folks, we'll follow up in email and update the pilot kanban. bye.
[36:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some names and acronyms were slightly off in auto-transcribe; manual corrections added in parentheses.

References mentioned: SAML metadata link (to be sent), SOC2 snapshot (to be provided), sample-audit-schema.csv (to be provided).
